summary: Migrated build processing from FastAPI BackgroundTasks to Celery with persistence, retries, and dead-letter queue support
reason_for_change: FastAPI BackgroundTasks are in-process and not persisted - lost on server restart/crash. Celery provides persistent task queue with Redis backend for reliability and scalability.
implementation_details: 1. Created backend/tasks/build_tasks.py with run_build Celery task using BuildTask base class with retry configuration (max 3 retries, ack-late). 2. Updated backend/api/builds.py to use Celery delay() instead of background_tasks.add_task(). 3. Removed BackgroundTasks import and _run_build_background function (moved to Celery task). 4. Task handles WebSocket events via manager.emit(), credit management, and build state updates.
architecture_impact: Core architecture change - build pipeline now uses Celery instead of in-process BackgroundTasks. Enables horizontal scaling of build workers and persistence across restarts.
performance_impact: Improved - builds are queued and processed independently of HTTP request lifecycle. Workers can be scaled horizontally.
database_impact: None - same MongoDB collections used, task state persisted in Redis
backward_compatibility: Fully backward compatible - same API contract, build_id returned immediately, status queried via GET /builds/{id}
migration_requirements: Deploy Celery worker alongside backend. Redis must be available for task queue and results.
evidence: backend/api/builds.py line 121-122 uses run_build.delay() instead of background_tasks.add_task(). Celery task configuration in backend/celery_app.py routes to 'build' queue.
known_risks: Celery worker must be running for builds to complete. If Redis is unavailable, builds fail immediately with clear error.
rollback_plan: Revert to BackgroundTasks: change run_build.delay() to background_tasks.add_task(_run_build_background, ...) and restore BackgroundTasks import
